submitter: bugs_open/380 session — Go slice (practice-claims family + operating_history attestation + numeric-scan arming guard), 2026-08-24
rationale: bugs_open/380's deterministic half. The config slice (Council-Submitted e684fc8d: migrations 597/598/600/601) makes the LLM auditor run cold and the planner constrain factless sites; this slice adds the cheap, always-on instrument for the same defect class — first-person statements of PHYSICAL practice ('we test', 'we buy', 'we weigh', 'we receive samples', 'manufacturers send us…') on a site with no recorded operating history — and the record by which a real operating site declares that it does these things. OWNER DECISION 2026-08-24 (in-session, offered 'warning' vs 'error on register-less sites' vs 'defer'): ship at default severity WARNING — record, never refuse. Rationale the owner accepted: RFC_023 (owner 2026-08-12) makes a rule that can NEWLY REFUSE a contract change (architecture scope), and 'we test every tool' is NOT false-by-construction (claims_global.go:99-101's bar for the refusing fleet-wide set — a real reviews site does test tools; only an attestation separates true from invented), so unioning it into ScanAllBannedClaims would convert every consumer's blocker/refusal to fire on legitimate operating copy (leopardessconsulting.co.uk 'We test every workflow on our own sites' — TRUE). So: a SEPARATE entry point (ScanPracticeClaims, the ScanRegulatedClaims precedent), findings stamped Check='practice_claim', recorded at the gate under a per-step key practice_claims_severity (default warning; warning|error|blocker; invalid → warning + Warn), exempted only by a complete OperatingHistoryAttestation (attested_by, attested_at, evidence) stored in evidence_base.operating_history — the CGV-033 shape (a RECORD a person signs, not a flag). A fleet-wide flip to refusal is RFC_003 §8 Q1 — architecture review — and the mutation test TestPracticeFamilyIsNotInTheRefusingUnion pins that it cannot happen by accident. Two consequences on shared seams, both named: (1) ParseEvidenceBase's nil rule is widened so an attestation-only base parses non-nil (else the exemption silently never fires — the exact reasoning CGV-033 used for Regulated); (2) because a non-nil base with ZERO facts would ARM ScanUnregisteredNumbers at error severity and refuse every figure on the site (the bugs_open/364 class), the number scan's arming now keys on HasScannableRegister() = facts>0 || bans>0 at its THREE call sites (validate_page_content gate, discovery check, claimscan) — NOT inside ScanUnregisteredNumbers, because a pre-existing test (claims_series_test.go, the 364 lane's) scans against a deliberately empty base and that contract is kept. This also closes the latent hazard CGV-033's own widening introduced for a regulated-only register. MEASURED 2026-08-24: attestation-only registers fleet-wide = 0, so no live site's behaviour changes. CALIBRATION per claims_global.go's header: 12/12 must-catch (the owner's four garden-tools sentences lead), 20/20 must-allow (honest disclosures, negations, intentions, second/third person, copy-about-the-copy), and a dry run over the COMPLETE live corpus — 1,867 components, all active/deployed sites (the first export silently dropped 414 rows on a kubectl stream error; counted against the DB and re-exported): 12 findings on 6 sites — garden-tools.uk 7 (every one a sentence the owner named as invented), 3 true-practice on operating sites (the attestation case), 1 clear false positive ('how we test your idea', idea.uk — a service description; named in the file header as the shape the next calibration starts from), zero hedge suppressions. Precision acceptable at warning. Council scope note: cmd/config-key-audit's TestBudgetCronCountsLiteralMatchesTheRegistry fails at HEAD 111ee2314 on create_tool_component (4 vs 5) and deploy_tool_to_site (3 vs 4) — another lane's Optional keys without a check.py regeneration; this slice adds NO Optional keys (validate_page_content has no ActionInputSpec; practice_claims_severity is read from step config) and does not move the RFC_022 budget.

plan.summary: A deterministic first-person practice-claims family with an operating_history attestation exemption, recorded at warning through its own entry point (never the refusing union); ParseEvidenceBase keeps attestation-only bases non-nil; the unregistered-number scan arms on register CONTENT at its three call sites. Inert until an image rolls.

edits.symbol: OperatingHistoryAttestation, (eb).OperatingHistoryAttested, practiceClaims, practiceEvidence, ScanPracticeClaims, ScanPracticeClaimsWithSuppressed, hedgedPracticeMatch, PracticeClaimCount
edits.rationale: Cloned from claims_regulated.go (CGV-033), with the differences the header states: precision over recall (physical verbs with objects; use/compare/describe/explain/supply/serve/help/believe/recommend and 'our clients' excluded; P5 requires 'us'), findings stamped practice_claim, suppressors observable (negated via negatedClaimMatch; hedged by a preceding conditional within 24 bytes — RE2 has no lookbehind), and NOT unioned. Calibration recorded in the header.

edits.symbol: EvidenceBase.OperatingHistory; ParseEvidenceBase nil rule; (eb).HasScannableRegister; ScanUnregisteredNumbers doc comment
edits.rationale: An attestation-only base must parse non-nil or the exemption never fires (CGV-033's reasoning, extended). HasScannableRegister names the property the register-comparison scans actually need — CONTENT — so an attestation cannot arm the number scan. ScanUnregisteredNumbers's own nil-only contract is kept (a pre-existing test scans a deliberately empty base); the guard lives at the call sites.

edits.symbol: checkPracticeClaims, practiceClaimsSeverity; the checkClaims branch (call-site guard on the number scan)
edits.rationale: The gate records practice findings at the configured severity (default warning — never affects validity; persisted with the result) beside checkBannedClaims; suppressed matches are logged, the same visibility rule the negation guard has. The number scan's `if eb != nil` becomes `if eb.HasScannableRegister()`. No ActionInputSpec exists for this action, so no ConfigKeys/Optional declaration changes and the RFC_022 budget does not move.

Same call-site guard as the gate, so an attestation-only register cannot start reporting every figure at medium in the post-deploy audit. The practice family is deliberately NOT wired into this check yet (slice 2b, after the item-queue cost is measured against bugs_open/033).

edits.symbol: PRACTICE / practice-suppressed lines; practiceTotal; the number-scan guard
edits.rationale: The dry-run instrument prints the family's findings and its suppressions, counted separately and EXCLUDED from the exit code (the ATTRIB precedent): nothing in the platform refuses on them, so a dry run must not assert an authority the gate does not have.

The 12/20 calibration tables; every incomplete-attestation mutation fails for the reason it names; the attestation-only base survives parse and is NOT scannable (regulated-only too); the mutation test that makes unioning the family a red build with RFC_003 Q1 in the failure message; the exemption cannot widen to the regulated or global sets.

The four zero-fact registers all carry banned_claims and stay scannable.

validate_page_content.go:395-409: validity = blockerCount == 0 && errorCount == 0; warnings are counted and persisted, never affect `valid`. registry.go:861 `validate_page_content` has no ActionInputSpec (no ConfigKeys, no StrictConfig) — verified by grep for RegisterActionInputSpec("validate_page_content") = none.

claims.go:626-644 negatedClaimMatch looks BACKWARDS from the match start, so 'We do not test' never matches P1 at all (the negator sits between 'we' and the verb — structural exclusion, asserted in the must-allow table); 'Not once have we tested' matches and is suppressed as negated. RE2 has no lookbehind, hence the scan-then-filter hedge suppressor.

RULINGS: RFC_023 (owner 2026-08-12) — a rule that can newly refuse is a contract change; owner 2026-08-02 §2 — new authority on a shared seam ships as an opt-in field with the unsafe default OFF (practice_claims_severity, default warning); RFC_003 §8 Q1 open — the flip-to-refusal venue; CGV-033 (register/content-governance.md:276+) — the attestation shape and the ParseEvidenceBase widening precedent.
plan.risks: 1. At WARNING nothing refuses: a warning at the gate is a persisted issue and a claimscan line, and bugs_open/071 shows warning findings can go unread. This slice is the INSTRUMENT and the lever, not the closer — the cold LLM audit (597) is the closer and its findings reach a human via claims_unverified; the writer arm (599) is the prevention. Stated plainly so nobody reads 'warning' as protection. 2. False-positive shape is real and named: bare-verb 'we test' on a service description ('how we test your idea', idea.uk) — 1 of 12 on the full corpus. Precision is acceptable at warning; it would NOT be acceptable at blocker, which is another reason the default is warning and the flip is an architecture question. 3. True-practice sites (leopardess, loanandmortgagecalculator) will carry a warning until they record an operating_history attestation — the designed answer, and the 2026-07-29 §3 obligation to TELL those consumers is discharged by CONTRIB notes to their lanes. 4. ParseEvidenceBase widening: a base holding only operating_history now parses non-nil; every nil-keyed consumer was enumerated (validate_page_content gate, save_sections_claims_guard floor, section_editor_regulated_guard, rewrite_negations_action, save_page_meta_description_action, discovery check, tool_backend_provision, check_content_duplication) — each either scans banned claims (nil-safe, and an attestation adds no patterns) or is guarded by HasScannableRegister after this change; tool_backend_provision keys on `data ? 'facts'`, unaffected. 5. The guard is at CALL SITES, not one door: a future fourth caller of ScanUnregisteredNumbers could forget it. Recorded in CLM-026; the alternative (inside the function) broke the 364 lane's empty-base test and would have been a same-file passenger on their active work. 6. Shared-file coordination: claims.go is also the 364 lane's target (isExcludedNumber/unitSuffixRe); they are holding until this commit lands and will rebase — agreed in writing. 7. Image ordering: nothing in config depends on this Go; practice_claims_severity must not be SET on any live step until the image carrying practiceClaimsSeverity has rolled (an unknown key is ignored today, so setting it early is inert, not harmful — but it would read as configured). 8. The discovery-check and save-floor wiring are deliberately absent (slice 2b): wiring the discovery check files claims_unverified items into a 1,087-item queue with no surface (bugs_open/033) for every site with 'we test' copy — the measured count above is what that decision needs. 9. HEAD's config-key-audit parity test is already red for two other actions; this slice adds no Optional keys, but a reviewer running that package will see the failure — it is reported, not caused.
